chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan, from Bakr ibn Salih, from al-Hasan ibn Sa'id, from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Khazzaz and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, who said:

We entered upon Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) and we told him that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) had seen his Lord in the form of a well-proportioned young man of approximately thirty years of age. And we said that Hisham ibn Salim, Sahib al-Taq, and al-Maysami say that He is hollow to the navel and the rest is Samad (not hollow).

So he fell prostrating to God, then said: 'Glory be to You! They have not recognised You, nor have they declared Your Oneness; it is for this reason that they have described You (in such terms). Glory be to You! Had they truly recognised You, they would have described You with what You have described Yourself. Glory be to You! How could their souls incline them to liken You to others?! O God! I do not describe You except with what You have described Yourself, nor do I liken You to Your creation. You are worthy of every good; so do not place me among the wrongdoing people.'
Then he turned towards us and said: 'Whatever you can imagine as a thing, conceive of God as other than it.'

Then he said: 'We, the family of Muhammad, are the middle path — the extremist cannot reach us, nor can the follower outpace us. O Muhammad! Indeed the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family), when he looked at the Majesty of his Lord, was in the likeness of a well-proportioned young man of approximately thirty years of age. O Muhammad! My Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is far too exalted to be in the description of created beings.'

He (the narrator) said: I said, 'May I be your ransom! Whose legs were in greenness?' He said: 'That was Muhammad. When he looked at his Lord with his heart, He placed him in a light like the light of the Veils, until what was within the Veils became clear to him. The light of God — part of it is green, part of it is red, part of it is white, and part of it is other than that. O Muhammad! Whatever the Book (Quran) and the Sunnah testify for Him, we are the speakers of it.'

key_terms.الصَّمَدُ: Samad — Quranic attribute (112:2) meaning the Eternal, the Absolute, the One upon Whom all depend, commonly understood in classical theology as 'not hollow'
key_terms.النَّمَطُ الْأَوْسَطُ: The middle path — the Imam's description of Ahl al-Bayt as occupying the correct theological middle between extremism (ghuluww) and falling short (taqsir)
key_terms.الْحُجُبُ: al-Hujub — the Divine Veils; a theological concept referring to the screens of light between God and His creation
key_terms.سُبْحَانَكَ: Glory be to You — a formula of divine transcendence (tanzih), affirming God's absolute freedom from all deficiencies and creaturely attributes

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about describing God and the Prophet's vision of his Lord?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) was visited by two narrators who relayed a report that the Prophet Muhammad had seen God in the form of a young man, and that some prominent Shia scholars — Hisham ibn Salim, Sahib al-Taq (Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man), and al-Maysami — were describing God as physically hollow. The Imam immediately prostrated and offered a supplication of divine transcendence (tanzih), declaring that those who anthropomorphize God have neither truly recognized Him nor properly affirmed His Oneness. He then provided the authoritative clarification: the prophetic vision was of a form in which the Prophet appeared, not of God Himself, and that God is absolutely beyond all creaturely description. The Imam's teaching that 'whatever you can imagine as a thing, conceive of God as other than it' became a foundational principle of Shia Islamic theology.
word_analysis: the extremist/one who goes to excess

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Husayn Bin Al Hassan, from Bakr Bin Salih, from Al Hassan Bin Saeed, from Ibrahim Bin Muhammad Al Khazzaz and Muhammad Bin Al Husayn both said,

‘We went over to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Rezaasws and we both told himasws that Muhammadsaww saw hissaww Lordazwj in an image of a young man of approximately thirty years of age, and we said that Hisham Bin Alim and Sahib Al Taq and Al Maysami are saying that Heazwj is hollow to the navel and the rest is ‘Samad’ (Not hollow)’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> fell prostrating to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, then said: ‘Glory be to You<sup>azwj</sup>! They do not recognise You<sup>azwj</sup>, nor are they (acknowledging) Your<sup>azwj</sup> Oneness, therefore due to that, they are describing You<sup>azwj</sup> (as such). Glory be to You<sup>azwj</sup>! Had they recognised You<sup>azwj</sup>, they would have described You<sup>azwj</sup> with what You<sup>azwj</sup> have Described Yourself<sup>azwj</sup> with. Glory be to You<sup>azwj</sup>! How are they obliging themselves that they are resembling You<sup>azwj</sup> with others. O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I<sup>asws</sup> do not describe You<sup>azwj</sup> except with what You<sup>azwj</sup> Described Yourself<sup>azwj</sup> with, nor do I<sup>asws</sup> resemble You<sup>azwj</sup> with Your<sup>azwj</sup> creatures. You<sup>azwj</sup> are the Rightful of every goodness, therefore do not Make me<sup>asws</sup> to be from the unjust people’.
Then heasws turned around towards us, and heasws said: ‘Whatever you are imagining from a thing, so imagine Allahazwj to be other than it’.

Then He<sup>azwj</sup> Said: ‘We<sup>asws</sup>, the Progeny<sup>asws</sup> of Muhammad<sup>saww</sup> are of the median classification which neither can the exaggerator catch-up with us<sup>asws</sup> nor do the followers precede us<sup>asws</sup>. O Muhammad! (You are saying that) Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, when he<sup>saww</sup> looked at the Magnificence of his<sup>saww</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup>, He<sup>azwj</sup> was in a body of a youth of approximately thirty years of age. O Muhammad!  My<sup>asws</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Greater than He<sup>azwj</sup> would happen to be in a description of the creatures’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Who was it, whose leg was in green?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Muhammad<sup>saww</sup>, when he<sup>saww</sup> looked at his<sup>saww</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> with his<sup>saww</sup> heart, He<sup>saww</sup> was Made to be in Light similar to the Light of the Veils, to the extent that is was clear to him<sup>asws</sup> what was in the Veils. The Light of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, from it is green, and from it is red, and from it is white, and from it is other than that. O Muhammad! Whatever the Book (Quran) testifies for Him<sup>azwj</sup>, so we<sup>asws</sup> are the speakers with it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn abu ‘Abdallah has narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il from al-Husayn ibn al-Hassan from Bakr ibn Salih from al-Hassan ibn Sa‘id from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Khazzaz and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn they both have said the following.

“We met Imam abu abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.) and stated to him that Prophet Muhammad (s.a.) saw His Lord in the fashion of a full grown young man of thirty years and added that Hisham ibn Salim and Sahib al-Taq and al-Maythami say that He is hallow down to His navel and the rest is solid.

The Imam bowed down to a prostrating position and then said, ‘(O Lord), Glory belongs to you they have not recognized You nor have they acknowledged Your Oneness thus, they attribute to You such things. (O Lord, Glory belongs to You, had they recognized You they would have attributed to You what you yourself have attributed to Yourself and they would not have considered You similar to things other than You. O Lord, I do not attribute to You anything other than what You have attributed to Yourself and do not consider You similar to Your creatures. To You belongs all good. Do not place me among the unjust ones.’
The Imam (a.s.) then turned to us saying, “Whatever you may imagine (make Wahm of) consider Allah some thing other than it.”

He continued, ‘We, people of the family of the Prophet (s.a.), are the middle type and the criteria. Those who exceed can not catch up with us and those who follow can not go ahead of us. O Muhammad, when the messenger of Allah looked at the greatness of his Lord he was of the type of people as fully grown up as thirty years old people. O Muhammad, my Lord, the Majestic, the Glorious, is far greater than to be of the qualities of the creatures.”

The narrator has said that I said, “May the Lord take my soul for your service, who was the one with his feet in the green?” The Imam said, “He was Prophet Muhammad (s.a.) when looked at his Lord with his heart He placed him in the light like that of the Hujub so he can see what is inside the Hujub. Of the light of Allah some are green, red, white and others. O Muhammad whatever has confirmation in the book and the Sunnah we affirm it.”
